newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes firmer as traders seek direction.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes firmer as traders seek direction.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended the day firmer on Thursday and traders said the market was seeking fresh direction in the wake of hefty falls this month.
July Brent ended the day nine cents a barrel up at $17.44 after July gas oil closed earlier in the afternoon at $162.25 a tonne, a fall of $1.25 on the day.
Prices had drifted downwards from the highs near the close and IPE brokers said this was in response to mild losses in New York.

"The market is lacking a bit of direction at the moment," one dealer said. "We are at the stage where we are at the lower end of the range - we had sharp falls, we broke through the lows from last year, and there has just been no follow-through selling."
"There could be a little more fund selling left but to all intents and purposes, if people had wanted to sell, they would have done so by now."
Prices were also supported by fresh indications of a delay to Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

Antonio Monteiro, chairman of the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq, said late on Wednesday Baghdad would submit a new pricing formula for oil sales under the oil-for-food deal only after the agreement of a food distribution plan - which U.N. officials said would be completed around the end of the month.
The renewed plan came into force on June 8.
Some dealers played down the importance of the expected delay to the plan. "It has not had too much of an impact today," a broker said. "If you were short, it may have made you a bit nervous."
Traders said the delay was administrative and not political and therefore still likely to go ahead.
"They have still got the same amount of oil to sell," one said. "It just means they have got five months to sell it in, and not six months.

Sellers of North Sea crude oil were also encouraged after the clear-out of a raft of mid-week physical crude cargoes which had been overhanging the markets. "It seems to have solidified a little," one trader said.

Markets also appeared unruffled by news that Germany was considering selling 7.3 million tonnes of crude oil, some 20 percent of its strategic oil reserves, to help plug a hole in government finances. A decision was expected on the sale on July 11.
"It has not really been of too much interest to us," one broker said.
